- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), so reduce forecast peak values by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often overestimates the rate of increase; cap upward momentum at 2–4% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model delays correction; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
- Model tends to overestimate mean reversion in short-term (1–3 day) horizons; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, reduce forecast by 2–5% for the first 3 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model fails to correct; apply a “reversion buffer” by subtracting 1–3% from forecasted peak values if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast range by 10–20% to reflect lower confidence.
